column1: # spark-default — Spark's shipped canonical governance model (#470).
# ONE machine-readable authority for the ALLOWED SHAPES of a Spark-managed
# repository's GitHub governance: which label families exist, what each one
# means, how execution structure is expressed, and which surfaces Spark can
# provision or assess. It is NEVER an authority for project-specific judgment
# — that issue #12 is P0, or that #20 blocks #21, is the human's call and
# FORMAT — line-oriented, tab-separated, '#'-comment and blank-line tolerant,
# the same discipline as the plan skill's issue manifest. Records:
# A NEW GOVERNED LABEL FAMILY IS DATA. Add a `family` record and its `member`
# records here (or in an operator/project model) and every generic consumer
# picks it up — no schema code changes.
# CATEGORY NAMES ARE NOT OWNED HERE. The `issue.taxonomy` scalar preference
# already owns the category NAME SET across the shipped/operator/project
# tiers, and keeps owning it; this model owns each category's colour,
# description, cardinality, and requirement. The two shipped files are held
# in parity mechanically (`spark doctor`), so they cannot drift.

column3: Spark's shipped canonical repository governance model

column1: # --- Issue taxonomy: the one primary work category ------------------------

column5: Primary work category — exactly one per issue
New capability or user-visible behaviour
Something behaves other than as documented
Docs, references, and explanatory prose
Maintenance with no behaviour change
Deliberate cleanup of a known compromise
Investigation whose output is a decision
CI, tooling, and delivery plumbing

column1: # --- Priority: one of P0-P3 where active work needs a priority ------------
# Ordering semantics are the member DECLARATION ORDER below, most urgent
# first, stated as data rather than inferred from the label spelling.

column5: Execution priority — exactly one where priority is required
Architectural blocker — nothing meaningful proceeds until decided
Core north-star work
Important, not on the critical path
Nice-to-have / polish

column1: # --- Orthogonal routing signals: themes, never a category -----------------

column5: Orthogonal routing/safety signal — accompanies a category, never replaces it
Carries a semantic decision only a human can make
Needs explicit human approval before it may proceed

column1: # --- Disposition: the release decision recorded mechanically --------------

column5: Release disposition where an issue has no milestone
Deferred with a reason; revisit before a future milestone (roadmap-check disposition)
A milestone is release/outcome scope; a milestone titled vX.Y maps to the release whose version is X.Y.*
Native parent/sub-issue links are the hierarchy; a sub-issue is an issue, a parent is a container that closes last
Native blocked-by records a TRUE prerequisite only — what must be true before work can start
A "Blocked by #N" sentence explains a prerequisite; it never creates one
Preferred delivery order is the release-gate's sub-issue order — its own authority
Implementation linkage is a linked PR plus a closing keyword

column1: # --- Separations that must not be collapsed ------------------------------

column4: Delivery order is never manufactured from blocked-by; an edge added to express preference becomes a false blocker
Delivery order is never manufactured from priority; distorting P0-P3 to express sequence destroys both facts
A theme label never satisfies the exactly-one category requirement
A disposition label accompanies a category; it never replaces it

column1: # --- Repository governance surfaces Spark can provision or assess --------

column5: Issue forms; each must carry a category label and never the deprecated enhancement alias
Pull request template
The governed label families as they exist on the remote
The trunk protection policy Spark declares; applying it stays a human act
Release automation configuration

column1: # --- Enforcement requirements that can be assessed mechanically ----------

column5: Trunk requires a pull request and blocks force-push and deletion
The trunk ruleset requires the validation check the workflow actually publishes
The PreToolUse guard blocks force-push and pushes to trunk
The commit-msg hook enforces Conventional Commits
